A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same work and include Appendices A-H. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the arXiv stamp and the acknowledgment/reference area.

before.justification: v4 reports original simulations and semi-real calibration experiments using real covariates and simulated labels, including Tables 1-3 and the experiments in Appendix H.

after.justification: v5 retains the original simulations and semi-real experiments in Section 7 and Appendix H, including numerical ECE results and reliability diagrams.

M1.justification: The angular predictor, angle and sign estimators, Platt-scaling procedure, multi-index extension, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic distributions, pretrained representations, and UCI/OpenML covariates. The 20 extended benchmarks in Appendix H.3 already appear in v4; v5 only adds an acknowledgment concerning their inclusion.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: the uncalibrated predictor, Platt scaling, and isotonic regression retain their existing participation in Tables 1-3 and the figures.

E3.justification: Training, holdout, covariance-pool and test sizes, model settings, ECE evaluation, and simulated-label procedures are unchanged. Both versions use the true angle in the semi-real experiments.

E4.justification: The holdout-size convergence comparisons and robustness checks using Rademacher/uniform covariates and clipped-ReLU links are unchanged in Figures 1-4 and Appendix H.1.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the 5000 Monte Carlo trials for sign estimation in Section 7.1. No seed information, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-6 retain identical results. Both versions report in Appendix H.3 that angular calibration achieves the lowest ECE on 15 of 20 datasets, with mean ECE 0.026.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, calibration and optimality theorems, angle-estimation results, and proofs in Appendices A-F are unchanged, including the multi-index extension.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about provable high-dimensional calibration, Bregman optimality, and conditions connecting Platt scaling to angular calibration.

C2.justification: The discussions of unstable angle estimation on real covariates, non-Gaussian universality, and unresolved cross-index angle estimation remain unchanged in Section 7.2, Section 8, and Appendix F.

D1.justification: Implementation information, hyperparameters, sample sizes, covariance estimation details, pseudocode, and dataset identifiers are unchanged. v5 supplies no additional code or data access information.

R1.justification: The 94 references and research positioning are unchanged. Thanking Bin Yu for an experimental suggestion adds neither a cited work nor a revised relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Page 10 adds a sentence thanking Bin Yu for suggesting the UCI experiments reported in Appendix H.3. Page 1 updates the arXiv version/date stamp; all other prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Visual changes are confined to the updated margin stamp on page 1 and minor acknowledgment/reference reflow on page 10. All figures, tables, and appendix pages retain identical layouts.

improvement.justification: v5 adds acknowledgment for experiments already documented in v4 and updates its version stamp, with minor reference reflow. The methods, proofs, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so these editorial edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
